description: Patient walks 2 miles daily for exercise
presentation: A 71-year-old man with no prior lung disease develops productive cough episodes lasting more than four weeks almost every year, usually after a presumed viral illness. He walks 2 miles daily for exercise. He denies wheezing; his chest X-ray is normal, PFTs are pending, and he has a history of GERD managed with famotidine (PPIs were tried without relief). In the past, a short course of azithromycin temporarily relieved the cough, but it always recurs. Should I continue empirically prescribing azithromycin each time he coughs given the prior improvement?
